questions: Did line_loss_events stay at 0 on the oval and s-bend, and did the slalom drop from 1.0 to 0?
Did max_error fall below 0.06 m on any track? If not, does the robot leave the tape without losing sensor coverage (drift or turn-rate lag)?
Did steering_oscillation rise above 0.16? If yes with no line loss, the next step is y = 0.05 m.
With kp 5.0, does the s-bend progress rise above 0.04, and does any track complete?
If there is still no completion with zero line loss, is wheel_track 0.10 m with mass 0.6 kg the right next step?
feedback_request.what_to_report: Per track (oval, s-bend, slalom): completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors. Also the kp that gave the best rms_error with this 16 mm array, and which sensors carry most signal on the line.

intent: Hold the iteration 2 sensing (contiguous 16 mm footprints at ±0.048 m) so the line stays detected through the error zone. The Integrator's kp 5.0 controller is the only change, so this race tests whether controller gain fixes the s-bend drift that sensing no longer causes. Expect line_loss_events near zero on all tracks, max_error below 0.06 m, and progress above the 0.04 s-bend result of iteration 2. Completion is the real target; a first completion on the oval or s-bend would confirm the sensing fix.
learning: Iteration 2 showed that contiguous 16 mm footprints remove line loss on the oval and s-bend but not the off-track failure. The remaining error is not a detection gap. Next, separate controller gain from geometry: this race holds the 16 mm geometry and changes kp to 5.0. If the drift persists, the next lever is turn rate (wheel_track 0.10 m, mass 0.6 kg) rather than more sensors.
rationale: Iteration 2 (seven 16 mm sensors, contiguous at x = ±0.048 m, y = 0.03 m) removed line loss on the oval and s-bend (0 events on both), which supports the sensing-footprint hypothesis. It did not produce completions. The s-bend still ended off track with max_error 0.0611 m and progress only 0.04, so the robot now leaves the tape by drift or turn-rate lag rather than by losing sensor coverage. The slalom still shows one line-loss event per run and max_error 0.0628 m. Iteration 1 also changed kp, so the two iterations are not cleanly comparable, but the sensing evidence points to the footprint change as the useful part. Body width cannot help, because the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m for any allowed width. For this iteration I keep the geometry identical to iteration 2, because the Integrator has already built that package with kp 5.0. That isolates the controller-gain change against the same sensing. The fallbacks are set so the next geometry step follows the evidence: if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.16 with no line loss, move the sensor y offset to 0.05 m; if line loss is still above zero on the slalom, widen the span; if the robot stays off track with zero line loss, move to wheel_track 0.10 m with mass 0.6 kg to raise turn rate.
